analysis.summary: Morocco are strong favourites against co-hosts Canada in this Round of 16 clash at NRG Stadium, Houston. Morocco finished the group stage unbeaten (W2 D1, including a draw with Brazil) and beat the Netherlands on penalties in the Round of 32, with Ismael Saibari scoring in all three group games. Canada advanced on a narrow 1-0 win over South Africa but carry injury concerns at key positions and face a Morocco side that has historically dominated this fixture. Morocco have never lost to Canada across four meetings and eliminated Canada 2-1 at the 2022 World Cup.
analysis.home_form: Canada went D1-1 vs Bosnia, W6-0 vs Qatar (weak opposition), L2-1 vs Switzerland in the group stage, then beat South Africa 1-0 in the Round of 32 — four matches total: W2 D1 L1. Their headline goal tally is skewed by the Qatar result; against quality opposition they have managed at most one goal per game. Alphonso Davies played only 15 minutes as a substitute in the South Africa win while recovering from a hamstring issue, leaving his starting status uncertain.
analysis.away_form: Morocco went D1-1 vs Brazil, W1-0 vs Scotland, W4-2 vs Haiti in Group C — finishing second behind Brazil on goal difference — then beat the Netherlands 1-1 (3-2 on penalties) in the Round of 32. Unbeaten in all four matches; Saibari scored in each group-stage game (3 goals total) and is the standout attacking threat. Achraf Hakimi and Brahim Diaz have been consistently influential on the flanks. Bounou produced a critical save in the Netherlands game.
analysis.h2h: Morocco hold a dominant head-to-head record: 3 wins, 1 draw, 0 losses across four senior meetings. Results: Canada 1-4 Morocco (friendly, 1984), Canada 1-1 Morocco (friendly, 1994), Morocco 4-0 Canada (friendly, 2016), Morocco 2-1 Canada (FIFA World Cup group stage, Qatar 2022). Morocco have scored 11 goals to Canada's 3 across those four encounters. Canada has never beaten Morocco.
injuries_news: Ismael Kone (Canada, central midfield) is out of the tournament with a broken ankle — confirmed absence.
Alphonso Davies (Canada, left wing-back / captain) played only 15 minutes in the Round of 32 vs South Africa while managing a hamstring issue; starting status vs Morocco is unconfirmed.
No injuries or suspensions reported for Morocco ahead of this match (unconfirmed lineups as of analysis time).
key_factors: Saibari scored in every Morocco group-stage game (3 goals) and is in top form — he becomes Morocco's joint all-time World Cup top scorer with his third goal.
Hakimi's overlapping runs and combination play with Brahim Diaz on Morocco's right flank will repeatedly target Canada's left defensive channel, especially if Davies is not fully fit to start.
Canada's scoring record against quality opponents is modest: 1 goal vs Bosnia, 1 vs Switzerland, 1 vs South Africa — one goal per game at best against non-weak sides.
Morocco's compact mid-block, directed by Bouaddi and Amrabat in midfield, limits transition opportunities and should neutralise Canada's counter-attacking threat through David.
Historical precedent strongly favours Morocco — Canada has never beaten them, and their 2022 World Cup meeting went 2-1 to Morocco in the group stage.
NRG Stadium, Houston: July afternoon heat and high humidity will test both squads; Morocco's experience from similar conditions in Qatar 2022 could be an advantage.
Co-host crowd advantage may lift Canada emotionally but is unlikely to bridge the technical gap; Morocco are the more complete and experienced knockout-stage team.

value_notes: Morocco win (h2h away, odds 1.83): market raw implied probability is 1/1.83 = 54.6% for 90-min Morocco win. After normalising the 90-min h2h market (overround 6.2%) and redistributing the draw probability (~28.5%) to full-match outcomes assuming Morocco wins ~60% of extra-time scenarios, market-implied full-match Morocco win is approximately 68.6%. Model gives Morocco 77%, an edge of approximately +0.084 on Morocco — exceeds the 0.05 threshold. Note: the simple edge formula (model_prob minus 1/odds = 0.77 minus 0.546 = 0.224) overstates the economic edge because the h2h market odds reflect 90-min pricing; the real information edge after ET adjustment is approximately +0.08. Totals 2.5 under (odds 1.65, normalised implied 0.577): model gives 0.65 (edge +0.073 >= 0.05). Morocco score 1 goal per game vs quality opposition (Brazil, Scotland, Netherlands), and Canada averages 1 goal per game vs non-weak sides — modal scoreline is 0-1 or 0-2, both under 2.5. BTTS no (odds 1.89, normalised implied 0.50): model gives 0.62 (edge +0.12 >= 0.05). Canada's probability of scoring against Morocco's organised defence is estimated at approximately 38% given their limited output vs quality teams (1 goal vs Bosnia, 0 vs Switzerland at full time, 1 vs South Africa in R32) and Morocco's historical clean sheet record in this fixture (conceded 0 vs Scotland, 0 conceded to Canada in 2016). All three selections exceed the 0.05 edge threshold: Morocco h2h away (+0.08 adjusted), totals under 2.5 (+0.07), btts no (+0.12).
